promise: FTX is fine. Assets are fine.
description: The SEC complaint places Bankman-Fried's assurance about FTX assets on or about November 7, 2022 and alleges that customer assets had been diverted to Alameda.
evidence: SEC alleges the assurance was made while Bankman-Fried knew customer assets had been used by Alameda.

review.note: SEC complaint dates tweet on or about November 7, not November 8; remove exact 72-hour narrative. This is a present-tense assurance, not a dated future promise. Insolvency narrative and later convictions require separate judicial outcome source.

promise: The labor reforms will be completed by the time of the 2022 World Cup (as reported).
description: Amnesty documented continuing gaps in remedy for World Cup workers. Its November 2024 response to FIFA's legacy fund said that fund did not provide the requested compensation for exploited workers.
evidence: Amnesty distinguished a FIFA legacy fund from a worker-compensation programme.

review.note: Amnesty's November 2024 account says FIFA legacy fund excluded compensation for exploited workers; the record's launched-2023 compensation-fund claim is unsupported. Original Al Thawadi quotation/date and full kafala abolition claim need primary legal/interview evidence.

promise: Ad-free is a real part of the brand promise.
description: On Netflix's Q3 2021 earnings call, Hastings reiterated that Netflix would remain ad-free as 'a real part of the brand promise.' After subscriber losses, Netflix launched its ad-supported tier ('Basic with Ads') on November 3, 2022, and later killed its ad-free basic plan.
evidence: Hastings' Q3 2021 earnings call statement on ad-free brand promise
Netflix launched ad-supported tier 2022-11-03 and phased out ad-free basic plan in 2023

review.note: Search did not establish the alleged October 19, 2021 Hastings quotation. Netflix's primary launch notice supports a US advertising tier on November 3, 2022, but that launch date is not an original promise deadline. Do not infer a dated no-advertising guarantee from general brand rhetoric.
